subject: Human Body
title: The Pancreas: Enzyme Producer
description: One-minute skill: The Pancreas: Enzyme Producer.

hook.text: The pancreas is a dual-purpose organ. One half digests food. The other half controls blood sugar.

buildup.text: Its exocrine cells produce digestive enzymes: lipase for fat, trypsin for protein, amylase for carbs.

discovery.text: These enzymes are released as inactive precursors. They activate only in the duodenum to prevent self-digestion.

twist.text: In pancreatitis, enzymes activate prematurely inside the pancreas. The organ literally digests itself.

climax.text: The pancreas delivers the main digestive toolkit. Without it, no macronutrient group gets properly broken down.

punchline.text: One organ makes enzymes for fat, protein, and carbs.

quiz.question: Why are pancreatic enzymes released in inactive form?
options: They need stomach acid to work
To prevent the pancreas from digesting itself
